chapter: Chapter 6. Solids and the solid–liquid transition
title: The mechanism of plastic deformation

prose.text:
Atoms are the basic units of chemical elements.
Within the elastic range of small strains, the atoms in a crystal shift slightly from their original equilibrium positions.
The distances between atoms and their arrangement change slightly as a result.

After the load is removed, the atoms can return approximately to their original positions if no damage or other irreversible process has occurred.
This recovery differs from plastic deformation, which leaves a permanent change in shape.
prose.source_text: 晶体弹性形变时，原子彼此只有很小的移动.

prose.text:
As plastic deformation accumulates, the relative displacements of atoms or molecules in a crystal can reach many times their original spacing.
The crystal remains deformed after the load is removed.

Slip is the relative movement of parts of a crystal along particular planes.
When plastic deformation occurs mainly through slip, without fracture or a structural transformation, most of the crystal can retain its ordered arrangement.

Retaining a crystalline structure does not mean that every atom keeps its original neighbors or that the lattice, the crystal's repeating pattern of particle positions, contains no defects.
A crystal that has undergone plastic deformation is not completely unchanged.
prose.source_text: 当塑性形变时，原子或分子的位移可以超过它们之间距离很多倍. 然而，没有破坏物体的晶体结构.

prose.text:
The original textbook explains plastic deformation in terms of slip between layers of the crystal lattice.
Slip marks can appear on the surface of a single crystal under tension, as in Figure 91 a.
The stress produced by tension has a shearing effect along suitable crystal planes and directions, helping slip occur.

Figure 91 b shows the relative offset between lattice layers after slip, with Latin letters used consistently to label the panels.
This is a simplified lattice model of the result of slip.
The model does not mean that complete atomic layers in real crystals necessarily move simultaneously as rigid, orderly units.

A dislocation is a line defect in the ordered arrangement of a crystal.
Slip in real crystals often occurs through gradual, local motion of dislocations.
prose.source_text: 晶体点阵的各个层相对稍微滑动. 受到拉伸的单晶体如图91 а 所示. 可以很明显地看到各层滑动的痕迹. 各层滑动的过程如图91 б 所示.

prose.text:
The original textbook emphasizes that slip can begin locally, rather than occurring throughout the crystal's entire volume at the same time.
The textbook uses local groups of irregularly arranged atoms in the lattice to illustrate possible starting sites.

In real crystals, dislocations and other local structures affect how slip begins and spreads.
This illustration does not mean that all plastic deformation must begin in the same kind of "weaker group of atoms".

Different defects have different effects: some structures help local slip, while others obstruct dislocation motion.
The presence of defects therefore does not always make the entire crystal easier to deform plastically.
prose.source_text: 所有的晶体原子层的滑动是在个别部分开始，而不是在整个晶体的所有体积中，它们是在由于某种原因晶格点阵强度很小的地方开始. 例如，在点阵中可以有排列紊乱的个别原子群.

prose.text:
A polycrystal consists of many grains, each a small crystal.
When plastic deformation occurs mainly through slip, slip also occurs within each grain.
Different grains usually have different orientations, so the planes and directions along which slip occurs most easily also differ.

Neighboring grains must accommodate one another's deformation, and grain boundaries can obstruct slip.
On this basis, the original textbook explains that the stress needed to begin plastic deformation in a polycrystal can be greater than in a single crystal.
The textbook notes that this effect is more noticeable in fine-grained materials.

This comparison applies to the relevant materials and slip conditions.
It is not a universal rule that any polycrystal is harder to deform than a single crystal of any orientation.

Grain orientations are not necessarily completely random.
Material composition, orientations produced by processing, temperature, and loading conditions all affect the result.
A material cannot be judged solely by whether it is polycrystalline or fine-grained.
prose.source_text: 多晶体塑性形变时，在单个小晶体中，也发生点阵各层的滑动. 但是，在不同的晶体中，最容易滑动的方向是不同的，因为它们总是相对紊乱的. 因此，多晶体的塑性形变是在比单晶体更大的应力下开始，在微粒结构的材料中特别明显.

data.chapter: 第六章 固体和固-液转变
data.title: 塑性形变的机构

prose.text: 晶体弹性形变时，原子彼此只有很小的移动.
当塑性形变时，原子或分子的位移可以超过它们之间距离很多倍. 然而，没有破坏物体的晶体结构.
晶体点阵的各个层相对稍微滑动. 受到拉伸的单晶体如图91 а 所示. 可以很明显地看到各层滑动的痕迹. 各层滑动的过程如图91 б 所示.
所有的晶体原子层的滑动是在个别部分开始，而不是在整个晶体的所有体积中，它们是在由于某种原因晶格点阵强度很小的地方开始. 例如，在点阵中可以有排列紊乱的个别原子群.
多晶体塑性形变时，在单个小晶体中，也发生点阵各层的滑动. 但是，在不同的晶体中，最容易滑动的方向是不同的，因为它们总是相对紊乱的. 因此，多晶体的塑性形变是在比单晶体更大的应力下开始，在微粒结构的材料中特别明显.
